title: Self-driving attribution excludes failed reviews
problem: This property labels only events emitted inside the sandbox. Server-side stamphog_review_failed events omit it. Rollout monitors cannot isolate failures from this feature.
suggestion: Derive the flag from run.output in mark_review_failed. Add stamphog_self_driving_review and stamphog_review_run_id to the failure event.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** every analytics capture in the product — a repo-wide grep finds exactly two stamphog events: `stamphog_review_completed`, emitted from inside the sandbox by `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:815-817`, and `stamphog_review_failed`, emitted server-side by `mark_review_failed`.
**Found:** the new attribution flag reaches only the sandbox leg. It is written into `STAMPHOG_EXTRA_PROPERTIES` at `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:168-177`, which the engine merges onto its own completed event and LLM traces.
**Found:** the failure event's property set at `activities.py:868-874` is `stamphog_repo`, `stamphog_pr_number`, `stamphog_team_id`, `stamphog_runtime`, `stamphog_error` — no `stamphog_self_driving_review` and no `stamphog_review_run_id`, so there is no property and no join key to separate self-driving failures from human-PR failures.
**Found:** the data needed is already in hand at that point. `mark_review_failed` loads `run` at `activities.py:822`, and the same one-line derivation used elsewhere in the file (`bool((run.output or {}).get("inbox_review"))` at `activities.py:237` and `:451`) would supply the flag.
**Found:** the gap is widest exactly where it matters. A run that fails before the sandbox starts (context fetch, credential minting, clone) emits no completed event at all, so the failure event is the only record of it.
**Impact:** the failure rate of self-driving reviews — the primary risk metric for a rollout that lets stamphog review bot-authored drafts for the first time — cannot be computed from these events. The comment at `activities.py:173-174` states segmentation is the goal, and the failure half of the funnel does not meet it. Observability only: no user-facing behavior changes.
**Priority:** `consider` is the right level and is kept — this costs the team monitoring fidelity during a gated rollout, not correctness.

title: An older completed run can hide the latest failed re-review
problem: The query excludes failed runs before it orders by recency. An older completed run at the same head can then hide a newer failed re-review. This happens after same-head reviews, including a base retarget. The older approval may already be dismissed. A later receiver retry treats the old verdict as current and does not replace the failed review.
suggestion: Load the latest run at the head without excluding statuses. Restart it when it is queued. Create a replacement when its latest status is failed or superseded. Only return early when the latest run is live or delivered.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the dedupe query at `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1202-1210`, the status set in `products/stamphog/backend/facade/enums.py:19-33`, `_supersede_prior_runs` at `tasks.py:415-432`, the same-head re-review triggers (`_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` at `tasks.py:49`, base retarget at `tasks.py:832-863`), `dismiss_stale_approvals` at `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:266-306`, and the refire source `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:72-139`.
**Found:** the premise holds only in one shape, and that shape is reachable. `.exclude(status__in=(SUPERSEDED, FAILED))` runs before `.order_by("-created_at")`, so a COMPLETED (or GATED) run created earlier at the same `head_sha` wins over a newer FAILED one, and `tasks.py:1211-1221` returns without a replacement. An older *live* run cannot cause this, because `_supersede_prior_runs` (`tasks.py:415-432`) turns it into SUPERSEDED, which the same clause excludes.
**Found:** two runs at one identical head come from `reopened` or a base retarget — both pass the carve-out gate at `tasks.py:167` and both keep the head fixed.
**Found:** the earlier approval is indeed gone by then. A base retarget dismisses approvals at every head through `_retract_approvals_on_base_retarget` (`tasks.py:441-472`), and any same-head re-review dismisses every standing approval as its first activity (`activities.py:284-300`). A failed second run therefore leaves the PR with no stamp and no pending verdict.
**Found:** recreate-on-FAILED is an intended guarantee of this leg, not an accident — the parameterized case `failed_run_recreated_on_refire` in `products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py` asserts it. So this is a hole in that guarantee.
**Impact:** after a reopen or base retarget whose re-review fails, later receiver refires read the stale COMPLETED verdict as current and never re-review. The PR stays without an approval until a new head arrives. The stale-approval invariant itself is not broken — no approval stands over unreviewed code.
**Priority:** lowered to `consider`. Three conditions must coincide: a second run at the byte-identical head (only `reopened` or a base retarget for a bot-authored self-driving PR), that run failing, and a further TaskRun output save to refire the receiver. The common path — a failed run at a fresh head — recreates correctly. The consequence is a missing verdict, not a wrong or unsafe approval.

title: Trusted prompt always claims the PR is a draft
problem: A self-driving PR can receive another review after it becomes ready and gets new commits. This block still tells the reviewer that the PR is a draft. The prompt does not show the real draft state elsewhere. The false trusted context can affect the LLM verdict.
suggestion: Pass `pr.draft` to `_format_self_driving`. Include the draft guidance only when `pr.draft` is true. Add a prompt test for a ready self-driving PR.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the two paths that stamp `ReviewRun.output["inbox_review"]`, and how that value reaches the prompt: `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:144` (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`), `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110` (`process_inbox_pr_review`), then `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451` → `products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:131` → `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321` → `Pipeline.self_driving` → classification key at `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:477` → `reviewer.py:692`.
**Found:** no trigger path tests draft state. The webhook carve-out filters on head-changing action, bot author, repo-native branch, task linkage and the reviewer toggle only (`tasks.py:167-215`), and `_review_skip_reason` returns `"bot_author"` for a ready bot PR (`tasks.py:226-231`), so the carve-out still runs. The receiver leg filters on open state and head sha only (`tasks.py:1166-1174`). A self-driving PR that a person marked ready therefore starts a run with `self_driving=True` and `pr.draft` False on the next push, reopen, or base retarget.
**Found:** the prompt carries the draft state nowhere else. `_check_prerequisites` skips the draft issue for these runs (`review_pr.py:590`), so the gate lines never mention it, and the template at `reviewer.py:552-594` has no draft field. `stamphog_draft` at `reviewer.py:363` goes to analytics properties, not to the prompt.
**Impact:** on a ready self-driving PR the TRUSTED block asserts a false fact — "It is a draft on purpose ... draft state is not a caution signal for this PR" — inside the region the prompt labels as computed by deterministic gates. The block also frames the run as Inbox triage, while an approval on a ready PR counts toward required reviews at once. The model cannot detect the error, because nothing else in the prompt contradicts it.
**Priority:** lowered to `consider`. The false sentence is permissive: it tells the model not to treat draft as a caution signal, and a ready PR has no draft state to penalize, so no verdict change is demonstrable — only a mild leniency framing. The state also needs a ready flip followed by a new head event, which is off the main Inbox flow.

title: The fail-soft check can delay requests and flood error logs
problem: Every GET and PATCH response queries the separate Stamphog database. An outage can delay requests by the connection timeout before the circuit breaker opens. Once open, this handler logs a full exception for every settings request. This duplicates error traffic during a known degraded state.
suggestion: Cache this informational status briefly or load it through a separate request. Handle database availability errors as an expected unavailable state. Emit a sampled warning or metric. Keep unexpected exceptions visible.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the serializer method at `products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:71-81`, the facade query it calls, the product-DB engine and circuit breaker that back that query, and the frontend logic that calls the endpoint.
**Found:** `has_reviewable_repo_config` at `products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125` is a single `.exists()` on `StamphogRepoConfig`, scoped by `for_team`. It is one boolean EXISTS query, not a fan-out or an N+1.
**Found:** the stall the finding predicts is already bounded by shared infrastructure. `posthog/settings/data_stores.py:214-219` sets `connect_timeout = 3` on both product-DB aliases and pins them to `posthog.db_backends.failopen`. `posthog/db_backends/failopen/base.py:28-44` raises `CircuitOpenError` in microseconds once the breaker is open. `PRODUCT_DB_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED` defaults to on outside tests (`posthog/settings/data_stores.py:177-190`), and breaker state lives in Redis (`posthog/db_circuit_breaker.py:144-157`), so the whole pod fleet shares one open marker after 3 failures in a 30s window. The worst case is therefore about 3 seconds on a small number of requests, once, and then instant failure. The suggested per-request cache would duplicate this mechanism.
**Found:** the endpoint is not hot. `products/review_hog/frontend/reviewHogSettingsLogic.ts:954-956` loads settings once on scene mount, and lines 802 and 811 re-load only on a save failure. The 10s poll at line 758 drives `loadRecentReviews`, not `loadSettings`. The GET path already does heavier main-DB work through `seed_canonicals_tolerantly` at `products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:142`.
**Impact:** the predicted log flood needs a request rate this endpoint does not have. A stamphog DB outage produces a few `logger.exception` lines from users who open the Code review scene, not duplicated error traffic. The extra EXISTS query and the sampled-warning refinement are polish on a fail-soft path that already degrades correctly, which the validation bar treats as noise rather than a reliability defect.

title: Worker loss can permanently drop the initial review
problem: Celery acknowledges this task before execution by default. A worker exit can lose the only initial trigger. The idempotent recovery code will never run.
suggestion: Set acks_late=True and reject_on_worker_lost=True. The existing head-based deduplication makes redelivery safe.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the global Celery configuration, the dispatch chain into this task, the alternative paths that could stamp the PR, and the in-repo precedents for late acknowledgement.
**Found:** nothing raises the default. `posthog/settings/celery.py` sets no `CELERY_TASK_ACKS_LATE`, and `posthog/celery.py:84` loads settings under the `CELERY` namespace only, so Celery's default early ack applies to `process_inbox_pr_review` at `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109`.
**Found:** the dispatch is one-shot. `queue_inbox_pr_review` calls `.delay()` at `products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149`, and `_start_stamphog_review` at `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:224-234` only swallows broker-publish errors. No scheduled job reconciles a PR that never got a run.
**Found:** no other path performs the initial review. `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` returns empty unless the action is `synchronize`/`reopened` or a base retarget (`tasks.py:167`), so the webhook leg cannot stamp a freshly opened self-driving PR.
**Found:** the author's own comment at `tasks.py:1155-1157` states this leg "has no webhook redelivery behind it", which is why every transient GitHub or DB error retries instead of dropping. Worker loss is the single drop path those retries cannot cover.
**Found:** redelivery is safe, so the suggested flags carry no duplicate-review risk. The head-keyed dedupe at `tasks.py:1202-1221` returns early at a live or delivered head, and `_start_review_workflow` swallows `WorkflowAlreadyStartedError` (`tasks.py:377-380`). The task already depends on this property for receiver refires.
**Found:** direct in-repo precedent for the same task shape — `products/visual_review/backend/tasks/tasks.py:37-43` and `:119-125` set `acks_late=True, reject_on_worker_lost=True` on comparable GitHub-facing idempotent product tasks; `posthog/tasks/exporter.py:48` and `posthog/tasks/tasks.py:348-358` do the same.
**Impact:** a worker that dies hard (OOM, node preemption, a shutdown that is not warm) between prefetch and completion drops the only trigger, and the PR reaches Inbox triage with no stamphog verdict. A later `output` save on the TaskRun or a later push can still recover it, but neither is guaranteed — a self-driving PR that lands its work in one push and waits for triage gets neither.

title: Broker failures lose the review request
problem: The broker publish is the only record of this request. The caller logs and suppresses publish failures. A temporary broker outage therefore loses the review permanently.
suggestion: Create an idempotent pending-review row before commit. Publish after commit, and add a periodic task that republishes pending rows.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the caller that swallows the publish error, the sibling dispatch in the same trigger, Celery's publish-retry defaults in this repo, and the recovery paths that exist without a new mechanism.
**Found:** the suppression is deliberate and correct, not an oversight. `_start_stamphog_review` at `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:210-234` runs inside a `post_save` receiver on `tasks.TaskRun` (dispatched via `transaction.on_commit` at `receivers.py:131`), and its docstring states the broker being down must never surface into the saver. Letting the publish raise would break the agent's own run save — a much worse failure than a missed review.
**Found:** the sibling leg has the identical posture by design. `_start_review` at `receivers.py:237-273` also catches every exception around the Temporal workflow start. The whole inbox trigger is best-effort by construction, so an outbox table plus a periodic republisher for the stamphog leg alone would be a new durability mechanism inconsistent with the trigger it lives in.
**Found:** transient broker blips are already retried below this code. Neither `posthog/settings/celery.py` nor `posthog/celery.py` overrides `task_publish_retry`, so Celery's default publish retry policy applies and `.delay()` only raises after those retries fail. Losing the request needs a sustained broker outage — during which no Celery review could run anyway.
**Found:** two recovery paths already exist. The receiver re-fires on every later `TaskRun` save that carries the PR URL (`receivers.py:76-79`), and any later push re-reviews through the webhook carve-out (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:167`), which does not require a prior run.
**Impact:** the residual exposure is one skipped auto-stamp on a bot-authored draft during a broker outage, with no data loss and no stale approval (the stale-approval paths are separate). The proposed remedy — a new pending-review table, a write before commit, and a periodic republishing task — is disproportionate to that, and lands squarely in the overengineering class the criteria drop.
**Impact:** the cheap, in-convention durability gap on this path (early Celery acknowledgement on `process_inbox_pr_review`) is already reported separately, so dropping this one loses no actionable signal.

title: Child access can enable a parent project's approval toggle
problem: The endpoint authorizes access against the team ID in the URL. `_get_or_create` then writes the canonical parent team's settings row. A user with access only to a child environment can enable the parent's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` setting. That setting can gate real GitHub approvals.
suggestion: Authorize access against the canonical team before reading or writing settings. Reuse or extract Stamphog's canonical-team permission, including scoped PAK and OAuth team checks.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the permission stack `TeamAndOrgViewSetMixin` builds for this viewset, the team id `_get_or_create` writes under, how `for_team` resolves ids on the read side, and the two sibling products that already defend this boundary.
**Found:** the split is real. `posthog/permissions.py:237` authorizes `TeamMemberAccessPermission` against `view.team` (the raw URL team), and `AccessControlPermission` checks the same URL team at `posthog/permissions.py:835` then returns early for `INTERNAL` at line 843. `products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:101-104` then calls `resolve_effective_team_id(self.team_id)`, which returns `team.parent_team_id or team_id` (`posthog/models/scoping/manager.py:41-59`), so the row is created and updated under the parent team.
**Found:** no parent/child inheritance exists in the authorization layer. `effective_membership_level` reads `self.p._prefetched_access_controls.get(self.team.id, [])` (`posthog/user_permissions.py:202`) and matches only `resource_id == str(self.team.id)`. A private parent team and an accessible child environment therefore produce different verdicts for the same user.
**Found:** the write reaches the review trigger. `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py` calls `ReviewUserSettings.load(instance.team_id, acting_user_id)`, and `load` uses `cls.objects.for_team(team_id)`, which canonicalizes by default (`posthog/models/scoping/manager.py:118-131`). The row written through the child URL is the row the trigger reads before it calls `queue_inbox_pr_review`.
**Found:** the gap class is already recognized in this repo, so it is not speculative. `products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:107-143` adds `StamphogCanonicalTeamAccessPermission` for the same reason, with `test_child_scoped_api_key_cannot_reach_parent_rows` at `products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_api.py:107`. `products/logs/backend/presentation/views/metric_rules_api.py:72-82` repeats the same permission.
**Impact:** confirmed authorization gap. A logged-in org member with membership on a child environment but not on its parent project can create and update their own ReviewHog settings row under the parent project, including `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. The GET also discloses the parent project's `stamphog_connected` boolean.
**Priority:** lowered to `should_fix`, because two parts of the reviewer's account overstate the reach. First, `scope_object = "INTERNAL"` makes `_get_required_scopes` return `None` (`posthog/permissions.py:514-515`), and token auth is then rejected at `posthog/permissions.py:600-602` with "This action does not support personal API key access" — so the suggested scoped-PAK and OAuth checks are unnecessary here, and only the session-auth membership re-anchoring is needed. Second, the row is keyed on `user_id=request.user.id`, so the caller can only touch their own preferences; the GitHub-approval consequence needs a second independent condition, because `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` must first pick that same user out of the report's latest `suggested_reviewers` artefact.

title: Caller-writable PR URL can bypass Stamphog approval gates
problem: `TaskRun.output.pr_url` is caller-writable through the task output endpoint. This code checks only the user toggle before it queues Stamphog. It does not verify the task repository, PR author, head repository, or trusted run linkage. The queued task stamps `inbox_review`, which bypasses Stamphog's normal author and review-mode gates. Any team member can control Signals tasks. A member can point the run at another accessible PR and cause a real GitHub approval.
suggestion: Re-fetch `task_run_id` through the tasks facade before creating the review. Require a server-verified PR binding to the task repository. Also require a repository-native head and the exact expected bot author. Stamp `inbox_review` only after these checks pass. Add a boundary test that supplies a human or fork PR and verifies that no review starts.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** whether `output.pr_url` is really caller-writable, what the receiver hands to Stamphog, what `process_inbox_pr_review` verifies before it stamps `inbox_review`, and what that stamp turns off in the engine.
**Found:** `pr_url` is caller-writable by design. `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1770` protects only `{"pr_merged"}` as webhook-attested; `_apply_caller_output` at line 1773 drops nothing else, and its own docstring covers the case "when the caller points the run at a different `pr_url`". The write surface is `set_output` (`products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1102-1118`, `required_scopes=["task:write"]`) and the run PATCH path (`facade/api.py:2039-2044`).
**Found:** any team member can drive a signals task. `_ensure_task_accessible` uses `task_control_q` for control actions (`presentation/views/api.py:861-866`), and `task_control_q` admits any task whose `origin_product` is in `TEAM_VISIBLE_ORIGIN_PRODUCTS` (`products/tasks/backend/visibility.py:22-27,46`), which lists `Task.OriginProduct.SIGNAL_REPORT`.
**Found:** the save reaches the receiver. `set_task_run_output` calls `run.save(update_fields=["output", "updated_at"])` (`facade/api.py:2154`), so the `update_fields` guard in `handle_task_run_saved` passes and the trigger fires.
**Found:** the receiver leg verifies nothing about the PR. `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126-138` forwards only `pr_url`, and never compares it to `task.repository`, which it read at line 101. `process_inbox_pr_review` then parses the repository out of that caller-supplied URL (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1134`), resolves any synced and enabled config for it, checks only that the PR is open and has a head sha, and creates the run with `output={"inbox_review": inbox_review}` (`tasks.py:1223-1230`). No author check, no fork check, no task-linkage check.
**Found:** the asymmetry is decisive. The webhook leg does all of it — `_is_bot_authored` (`tasks.py:169`), head-repo equality against the base repo (`tasks.py:176-178`), and `find_signal_implementation_run` with a team recheck (`tasks.py:191-200`). The receiver leg has none of these, and it is also the leg that never evaluates `_review_mode_skip_reason` or `_author_lacks_write_permission`, which live only in `process_pull_request_event` (`tasks.py:944`, `tasks.py:968`).
**Found:** the stamp is what matters. `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451` sets `self_driving_review` from `output["inbox_review"]`; `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:324` then skips `_refuse_bot_author`, `review_pr.py:590` skips the draft prerequisite, and `reviewer.py:683-700` injects a TRUSTED provenance block asserting the PR is "verified by task linkage" — an assertion this leg has not established. The comment at `activities.py:448-450` claims both trigger paths stamp "only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run"; on this leg that claim is false.
**Found:** the current master version of the same function adds precisely these checks — a `repository` parameter with a mismatch refusal, `_is_self_driving_pr(pr, repo_config.repository)` under the comment "TaskRun.output.pr_url routed us here and any team member can write it, so re-verify author and head against GitHub", and a head-ref binding to the branch stamped into protected run state. That is independent confirmation of the same defect and of the fix shape.
**Impact:** a team member can PATCH a signals run's `output.pr_url` to any open PR in a repository the team has already connected to Stamphog, and that PR is then reviewed with the bot-author refusal, the draft prerequisite, the review-mode gate, and the author-write-permission gate all inactive. An approve verdict posts a real GitHub approval, which is the exact stale-approval and bot-author boundary `products/stamphog/CLAUDE.md` documents as an invariant.

title: The PR URL parser accepts embedded GitHub URLs
problem: The regex searches for `github.com` anywhere in the input. For example, `https://evil.example/github.com/acme/repo/pull/7` selects `acme/repo` and triggers a privileged GitHub request. This violates the function's GitHub PR URL contract.
suggestion: Parse the URL with `urllib.parse.urlparse`. Require HTTPS, an exact `github.com` hostname, no credentials, and an exact `owner/repo/pull/<positive integer>` path. Reject query strings and fragments.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** every caller of `_parse_pr_url`, how the parsed slug is used afterwards, and the full chain that supplies `pr_url`.
**Found:** `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130` is the only call site. The parsed slug is a lookup key and nothing else: `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1147` selects a `StamphogRepoConfig` for the team with `repository__iexact=repository, enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False` and a non-blank `installation_id`, and returns at `:1151-1153` when no such config exists.
**Found:** the GitHub call at `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1159` uses `repo_config.repository` and `repo_config.installation_id`, not the strings taken from the URL. The URL is never rendered to a user and never becomes a request target. So the reachable repository set is exactly the team's own connected and enabled Stamphog repos.
**Found:** `pr_url` reaches the task from `TaskRun.output["pr_url"]` at `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93`, through `_start_stamphog_review` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:210`) and `queue_inbox_pr_review` (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128`). Whoever can write that field can write a well-formed `https://github.com/<connected-repo>/pull/7` just as easily as the embedded-URL variant, and both reach the same code path with the same result.
**Impact:** The proposed strict parse removes no capability. The example input selects a repository the team already connected, which a plain GitHub URL selects too, so it grants no new access and mints no request an attacker could not already cause. This is hardening against an input shape that changes no outcome, so it does not meet the security or correctness bar.
**Impact:** The strict parser that exists at `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1940` is not a counter-example. It guards a URL that is rendered into an outbound email, and it binds the URL to `run.task.repository`. Neither property applies here, where the config lookup is the real bound.

title: Do not trust an unbound context flag to bypass approval gates
problem: run() treats any truthy self_driving_review value as trusted proof. It then disables the bot-author and draft gates. The upstream receiver stamps this value without verifying the PR author, head repository, or supplied task linkage. A caller can point an eligible task run at another PR in the configured repository. Stamphog can then review that PR without its normal label and author gates. The prompt also presents the unverified provenance as trusted.
suggestion: Validate the attestation before Pipeline construction. Require self_driving_review to be exactly true. Reload task_run_id and verify its team, signal report, repository, and PR binding. After the GitHub fetch, require a bot author and a repo-native head. Pass provenance bound to the PR number and head SHA. Fail closed on any mismatch.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the full provenance chain behind the flag — `review_local.py:321` reads `self_driving_review` from the context JSON, which only the server writes (`products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:131`), from `bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` at `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451`. The context file is rendered before the sandbox starts the engine, so no code inside the sandbox can set or flip it, and the value is already a Python bool — `is True` instead of `bool(...)` changes nothing.
**Found:** `ReviewRun.output` has no write path from the API. The viewset exposes it through a read-only `SerializerMethodField` over an allowlisted subset (`products/stamphog/backend/presentation/serializers.py:329-341`). Only the two Celery trigger paths stamp `inbox_review` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1064` and `:1229`).
**Found:** the task linkage the finding calls unverified is verified upstream on the receiver leg. `handle_task_run_saved` fires only for a run whose task carries `signal_report_id` and is not internal (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:98-105`), passes `instance.team_id` (`receivers.py:121,135`), and checks the acting reviewer's toggle (`receivers.py:114-126`). Stamphog then resolves a synced and enabled config for the PR's own repository inside that same team (`tasks.py:1140-1147`), so a cross-tenant bind is not possible.
**Found:** the PR the receiver forwards is `TaskRun.output["pr_url"]` — the run's own recorded PR, not a caller argument. The single caller of the facade is that receiver (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128`, `receivers.py:225`). In this repository the only writer of `output.pr_url` is the GitHub webhook backstop, which requires a branch and repository match to the run and refuses fork heads (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:64-78,178-185`). No endpoint accepts a caller-supplied `output.pr_url`.
**Impact:** the described attack has no reachable actor. To point an eligible run at an unrelated PR, the attacker must already write `TaskRun.output` — that is the internal agent server or the database, both inside the trust boundary. An outside party cannot use the fork route, and a repository collaborator gains nothing, because they can apply the trigger label themselves.
**Impact:** one real asymmetry remains — the receiver leg does not recheck bot authorship or a repository-native head, which the webhook carve-out does (`tasks.py:169-178`). Its consequence still depends on a trusted internal writer recording a wrong PR URL, and the product identifies self-driving PRs by task linkage rather than author login by design, so this stays a speculative chain rather than a demonstrable authorization gap. It does not meet the bar, and `must_fix` overstates it by a wide margin.

title: Stamphog ignores opted-in secondary reviewers
problem: The gate checks only the single canonical reviewer. A second assigned reviewer can enable Stamphog, but the initial review still does not start. The webhook resolver repeats this error for later commits. This conflicts with the requirement that any assigned reviewer can enable reviews.
suggestion: Resolve all assigned reviewers in their current order. Prefer the assigned task creator when that user opted in. Otherwise, select the first opted-in assigned reviewer. Use this selection for both the initial dispatch and the webhook resolver. Add coverage where the canonical reviewer opts out and a second reviewer opts in.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** how the acting reviewer is resolved, whether the toggle check runs per-reviewer or per-report, whether the two dispatch paths agree, and how the current master version of this file resolves the same question.
**Found:** the resolution collapses the reviewer set to one user before any toggle is read. `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:203-207` builds the ordered `resolved` list and then returns a single id: `acting = next((user for user in resolved if user.id == task_created_by_id), resolved[0])`. The `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` value of every other resolved reviewer is never loaded.
**Found:** both call sites read only that one user's row. `receivers.py:114` loads `ReviewUserSettings.load(instance.team_id, acting_user_id)` and line 126 gates the Stamphog dispatch on it; `receivers.py:151-155` repeats the same single-user lookup for the webhook resolver.
**Found:** the fallback makes the miss common, not rare. The docstring at `receivers.py:167-169` records that background signals tasks are created as the GitHub-integration creator, which carries no assignment meaning. That creator is normally absent from the resolved set, so `resolved[0]` — whoever the report happens to list first — becomes canonical, and any other assignee who flips the toggle gets no review.
**Found:** the current master version of this file resolves it exactly as the suggestion describes: `_resolve_assigned_reviewers` returns the list, `_pick_reviewer` keeps canonical-reviewer semantics for the ReviewHog leg, and a separate `_pick_stamphog_reviewer` picks among the opted-in reviewers with the task creator preferred while still opted in. Its comment states the reason — stamphog reads no per-user options, so narrowing to one reviewer would drop reviews the other assignees asked for. Both the initial dispatch and the webhook resolver use that same selection.
**Impact:** confirmed functional defect. An assigned reviewer who enables the toggle gets no Stamphog review whenever a different assignee is canonical, and the same narrowing applies to re-reviews on later pushes. There is no error or log to explain the silence.
**Found (correction):** in this branch the two paths use identical logic, so they do not currently disagree. The extra hazard master's comment warns about — one path firing on "any assigned reviewer opted in" while the other gates on the canonical reviewer, which would retract a standing approval while somebody is still opted in — appears only if the initial dispatch is widened and the webhook resolver is not. That is why the suggestion's "use this selection for both" is load-bearing.

title: Self-driving provenance is granted before the PR is verified
problem: The initial task marks every open PR from a configured repository as `inbox_review`. It does not load `task_run_id` or compare `signal_report_id`. It also does not check the head repository or the configured PostHog Code bot identity. The webhook path uses `_is_bot_authored`, which accepts every bot account. An incorrect task output can therefore grant the self-driving bypass to an unrelated human, fork, or third-party bot PR. This bypass disables the bot and draft gates and can post a GitHub approval.
suggestion: Create one fail-closed provenance verifier and use it on both paths. Validate the exact task run, team, report, repository, PR URL, head repository, and configured PostHog Code bot login. Use `GitHubIntegrationBase.parse_pull_request_url` so non-GitHub hosts do not match. Stamp `inbox_review` only after all checks pass.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** every gate applied on each of the two trigger legs, where `inbox_review` provenance is consumed, and who writes the `pr_url` the receiver leg trusts.
**Found:** the three webhook gates exist only on the webhook leg — `_review_skip_reason` at `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:870`, `_review_mode_skip_reason` at `:944`, `_author_lacks_write_permission` at `:968`. `process_inbox_pr_review` (`:1130-1234`) calls none of them, never reads `pr["user"]` or `pr["head"]["repo"]`, and never compares the URL's repository against the task's own `repository`. It stamps `output={"inbox_review": inbox_review}` at `:1229` for any open PR whose slug matches a connected and enabled config.
**Found:** that stamp is the only input to the engine carve-out. `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451` sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`, and its comment at `:448-450` states both trigger paths stamp "only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run" — true for the webhook leg, false for this one. Downstream the flag skips the bot-author refusal (`tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225`), skips the draft gate (`:590`), and injects the TRUSTED provenance block (`tools/pr-approval-agent/reviewer.py:683-701`) that tells the model author familiarity and org membership carry no signal.
**Found:** the `pr_url` is caller-attested, not GitHub-attested. `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93` takes it from `TaskRun.output["pr_url"]`, and `_apply_caller_output` (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1769-1786`) attests only `pr_merged`, with a docstring that names a `task:write` holder as the threat model for run output. The same repository already distrusts this exact field elsewhere: `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1940-1972` parses it with `urlparse` and requires it to match `run.task.repository` before an email goes out.
**Impact:** a wrong or manipulated `output.pr_url` on a signals run whose acting reviewer opted in selects any open PR in any of that team's connected repos. That PR then gets a hosted review carrying self-driving trust, past the draft gate, past `review_mode`, and past the author write-permission gate — the gate `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:100-107` says exists so an under-privileged author cannot obtain an approval that satisfies branch protection. The verdict can be a real GitHub approval on a human or fork PR nobody vetted.
**Impact:** no test covers the gap. `products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:909-944` exercises only a bot-authored draft on this leg, while the webhook leg has `test_inbox_carve_out_requires_task_linkage` at `:875`.
**Impact (accuracy note for the author):** two sub-claims in the finding are weaker than the core. `task_run_id` and `signal_report_id` come from the same `TaskRun` as the `pr_url` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:130-138`), so those ids are self-consistent by construction; and the loose `_is_bot_authored` is not the hole on the webhook leg, because `find_signal_implementation_run` at `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:191` supplies the linkage there. The real defect is the receiver leg performing no PR-side verification at all.

title: Canceled implementation runs still qualify for the carve-out
problem: find_task_run can return FAILED or CANCELLED runs. This facade does not reject those states. A later push can therefore bypass the bot and draft gates for an abandoned task.
suggestion: Return None when the matched run has FAILED or CANCELLED status. Add facade tests for both states.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** what `find_task_run` can return and why, what the carve-out does with the returned run, and what rejecting terminal runs would change for a live self-driving PR.
**Found:** returning a terminal run is deliberate, not an oversight. The pr_url leg ranks non-terminal runs first (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:46-57`), so a terminal run surfaces only when no live run claims the PR, and the docstring at `products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:37-40` plus the comment at `:83` state that terminal runs must stay matchable because post-merge events for bound runs resolve through this leg.
**Found:** run liveness is not what the carve-out trusts. `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-178` already requires a bot-authored PR whose head repo equals the base repo before any lookup runs, so a human PR pushed onto a dead run's branch never reaches the facade. The run match answers "is this PR a PostHog Code PR from an Inbox report", and a later FAILED or CANCELLED status does not change that fact about the PR.
**Found:** the proposed rejection would break live PRs. Successful signals runs deliberately stay `in_progress` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:5-7`), so "terminal" here means failed or cancelled — including the ordinary cloud-to-local handoff, which marks the run cancelled at `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2104`. After a handoff or a post-PR agent failure the PR is still open and still receives pushes; rejecting the run would stop re-review and route each push to the skip path, which dismisses the standing approval with the untrusted-author message. That is a functional regression, not a tightening.
**Found:** the early return on FAILED/CANCELLED at `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:90` is not a precedent for this. It stops a failed run's own output save from starting a review; it does not declare a PR untrusted because its run later ended.
**Impact:** no concrete harm follows from the matched run being terminal — the PR is the same bot-authored, repo-native, team-scoped, toggle-gated PR either way, and the gates the carve-out bypasses are bypassed for exactly that shape. The finding names a trigger but not a consequence, so it does not meet the bar.

title: Report-linked discussion tasks are classified as implementations
problem: The function treats every non-internal task with `signal_report_id` as an implementation task. The Tasks API also supports non-internal discussion and other report-linked tasks. Only real implementation tasks have the durable `relationship="implementation"` link. A PR from a discussion task can therefore bypass the standard bot, draft, review-mode, and permission gates.
suggestion: Check `Task.OriginProduct.SIGNAL_REPORT` and the durable implementation relationship before returning the DTO. Use `SignalReportTask.relationship == "implementation"` or the typed implementation artefact that existing Signals code uses. Return None for other report-linked tasks.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** every writer of `Task.signal_report_id`, the API surface that creates report-linked tasks, the relationship vocabulary and what it actually gates, and how the two stamphog trigger legs define "self-driving".
**Found:** the factual premise holds — the Inbox UI really does create non-internal `discussion` tasks. `frontend/src/scenes/inbox/types.ts:232-239` defines the vocabulary as `implementation` and `discussion`, and `frontend/src/scenes/inbox/inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:80-95` posts `origin_product=SIGNAL_REPORT` plus `signal_report` for both buttons. Such a run therefore matches `find_signal_implementation_run`.
**Found:** the relationship label is client-asserted free text, so it is not a trust anchor. `products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:442-448` accepts any string matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` straight from the caller, and `products/signals/backend/task_run_artefacts.py:148-149` writes the `implementation` row whenever the caller omits the field. Anyone able to create a `discussion` task can create an `implementation` one instead, so the proposed check stops nobody and is not a permission boundary.
**Found:** the extra matched class has the same trust shape as an implementation PR. The kickoff starts the run with `run_source=signal_report`, which the comment at `frontend/src/scenes/inbox/inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:90-93` states makes any PR bot-authored server-side. The carve-out still requires a repo-native head (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:176-178`), a synced and enabled config for that repo (`:179-186`), team scoping inside the facade (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504-506`), and an acting reviewer whose toggle is on (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:201-207`). Same bot, same repo, same team, same opt-in.
**Found:** the two legs share this definition deliberately. review_hog's receiver leg gates on exactly `internal` plus `signal_report_id` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:98-105`), which predates this PR, and the facade docstring (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:489-497`) says it matches the same way. Tightening only the facade would let the initial review run and then stop every re-review, so each later push would dismiss the standing approval with the untrusted-author message — a regression the suggestion does not account for.
**Impact:** the worst confirmed outcome is that a discuss task which ends up opening a PR gets reviewed under the same provenance as an implementation PR. That matches the toggle's stated purpose, and no gate is crossed that the actor could not cross anyway by labeling the task `implementation`, so the claimed bypass does not hold and the finding does not meet the bar.

title: A broker failure permanently drops the initial review
problem: This call is the only initial review trigger. The exception handler only logs a publish failure. A transient broker outage can therefore lose the review after the TaskRun output commits. The task retry policy cannot help because Celery never received the task.
suggestion: Persist the dispatch intent before publication. Let a worker retry it until Celery accepts the task. Use task_run_id as the idempotency key. A scheduled reconciler can provide the same recovery if an outbox is not suitable.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** whether the dispatch is genuinely single-shot, what re-dispatch paths exist, whether the queued task tolerates repeat dispatch, and whether the maintainers treat this catch as deliberate.
**Found:** re-dispatch is a designed, load-bearing property, not an accident. `handle_task_run_saved` fires on every `TaskRun` save whose `update_fields` include `output` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:88-91`), and the module docstring at lines 78-84 records that repeat saves with an unchanged target re-fire deliberately. `process_inbox_pr_review` states the same contract from the other side: "The receiver re-fires on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL" (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1124-1128`). Every later `set_output` or run PATCH by the agent server re-enters this path with the same `pr_url`.
**Found:** the idempotency the suggestion asks for already exists, in a stronger form than a `task_run_id` key. `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1198-1221` dedupes under a row lock on `(pull_request, head_sha)` against the PR's current head, restarting a stranded QUEUED run rather than duplicating it. A recovered dispatch is therefore safe, and a dispatch after new commits reviews the new head instead of being suppressed.
**Found:** a second recovery path covers the same PR. Later pushes, reopens, and base retargets re-review through stamphog's webhook carve-out (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:144-215`), which GitHub redelivers on failure. PostHog Code PRs normally take follow-up commits, so a lost initial publish is usually superseded by the first push.
**Found:** the catch is a deliberate, pre-existing convention, not something this change introduces. `receivers.py:213` states the intent — the broker being down must never surface into the saver — and the sibling ReviewHog dispatch `_start_review` uses the identical swallow-and-log against Temporal. The current master version of this file keeps both unchanged, including the same `except Exception: logger.exception(...)` in `_start_stamphog_review`, while it does rewrite the reviewer resolution and add a repository argument. The maintainers revisited this function and left this shape.
**Found:** the error is logged at `receivers.py:233-234` with `logger.exception`, so this is not a swallowed failure that hides itself. Celery's default `task_publish_retry` also retries the publish itself, which absorbs a momentary blip before the handler is ever reached.
**Impact:** the residual gap is narrow and fails closed. It needs a broker outage that outlasts the publish retries, landing exactly on the PR-URL save, on a PR that then receives no further commits and whose run saves no further output. The result is a missing draft-time opinion, never a wrong verdict and never an approval over unreviewed code. Against that, the proposed remedy is a new persisted-intent outbox or a scheduled reconciler for an opt-in, best-effort review — disproportionate to the risk, and duplicating recovery the head-keyed dedupe and webhook leg already provide.

title: Eligibility filters run after selecting one task run
problem: find_task_run selects one run before this facade applies team and signal filters. Another matching run can hide the valid signal run. The webhook then skips every later review for that pull request.
suggestion: Apply team_id, signal_report_id, and internal filters before .first(). Extend find_task_run with these filters or build a scoped query here.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** both legs of `find_task_run`, the default ordering they inherit, how the signals run comes to hold the PR URL before the carve-out ever runs, and what the caller does when the facade returns None.
**Found:** neither leg picks an arbitrary row. The pr_url leg orders non-terminal first then `-created_at` (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:46-57`), and the branch leg inherits `TaskRun.Meta.ordering = ["-created_at"]` (`products/tasks/backend/models.py:1146`), so "another matching run" means a newer run, not a random one.
**Found:** by construction the signals run is always a candidate on the pr_url leg. The stamphog leg is only ever queued from `TaskRun.output["pr_url"]` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93` and `:126-138`), so the run that produced the PR already stores that exact URL by the time a later webhook delivery calls the facade. Every other run of that same task shares its `team_id` and `signal_report_id`, so the post-filter at `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:505-509` passes whichever of them wins the ordering.
**Found:** for the race to hide the signals run, a run on a *different* task must carry the identical `output.pr_url` for the same repository. The webhook backstop cannot produce that state: `_record_run_pr_url` writes the field only when it is unset (`products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:203-212`) and resolves through the same pr_url-first lookup, which already returns the signals run. That leaves only a caller writing another task's PR URL by hand into its run output.
**Found:** the branch leg is effectively unreachable here for the same reason — it runs only when no run stores this PR URL, which contradicts the precondition that queued the feature in the first place.
**Impact:** the failure degrades closed, not open. `None` produces an empty `_InboxCarveOut` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:199-200`), the delivery falls through to today's skip path, and that path still retracts the standing approval (`:894-898`). No approval survives over unreviewed commits; the cost is one skipped re-review in a state the normal flow prevents.
**Impact:** the shared matching rule is deliberate — `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:489-492` states it matches runs the way the webhook backstop does. Scoping the search itself would let the two paths disagree about which run owns a PR, so the suggestion trades a rare fail-closed miss for a new inconsistency. This does not meet the bar.

title: Record hosted WAIT outcomes for self-driving reviews
problem: Flagged bot PRs now pass the refusal at line 324. If a reviewer bot still has a fresh 👀, `run()` returns `WAIT` without calling `_capture_review_completed()`. The Action path records this outcome in `_handle_in_flight_bot_reviews()`. Hosted completion data will omit these waits. This hides retry pressure and weakens rollout monitoring.
suggestion: Call `pipeline._capture_review_completed("SKIPPED", "WAIT")` before the return. Add a regression test for a flagged bot PR with a fresh 👀.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the actual PR diff for `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py` (`gh pr diff 75215`). It changes exactly two lines in `run()`: the `Pipeline(...)` construction and `if pipeline.pr.author_is_bot and not pipeline.self_driving:`. The in-flight WAIT block at `review_local.py:338-351` is untouched, pre-existing code.
**Found:** the missing capture is therefore not introduced here and is not specific to bot PRs. Every hosted run — human-authored ones included — has always returned WAIT from that branch without `_capture_review_completed`. The carve-out only lets one more author class reach an unchanged branch that behaves identically for it.
**Found:** the hosted WAIT outcome is durably recorded server-side, so retry pressure is not invisible. `post_verdict` writes `run.verdict = parsed.verdict` with `status = COMPLETED` for the non-approve branch (`products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:757-761`), and the gate-blocked branch sets `ReviewVerdict.WAIT` explicitly (`activities.py:721-722`). `ReviewVerdict.WAIT` exists in `products/stamphog/backend/facade/enums.py:41` and the run rows are exposed through the review-runs API. The gap is limited to the engine's `stamphog_review_completed` analytics event.
**Impact:** the confirmed consequence is one analytics event missing on a rare tail path — the server's bot-wait budget must expire with a reviewer bot still holding a fresh 👀 — while the same outcome stays queryable in the product DB. That is a telemetry-consistency nit in unchanged code, not a correctness, contract, data-loss, or reliability defect, so it does not meet the bar. The claim that it is directly related to the changes does not hold up against the diff.

title: Child-environment PRs never receive Stamphog re-reviews
problem: Stamphog calls this hook with the canonical parent team ID. Task runs and signal reports can retain a child environment ID. The Tasks facade rejects that mismatch before this hook runs. The artifact query would also search with the wrong ID. The initial review succeeds, but later pushes never receive re-reviews.
suggestion: Compare canonical IDs for tenant ownership. Then call this resolver with the raw `run.team_id`. Add a test where the task belongs to a child environment and the Stamphog config belongs to its parent.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** which side of this join canonicalizes `team_id`, whether the comparison in the tasks facade tolerates a raw-versus-canonical pair, why the initial leg still works, and what the webhook path does when the carve-out comes back empty.
**Found:** the two sides store different ids by construction. `StamphogRepoConfig(ProductTeamModel)` (`products/stamphog/backend/models.py:24`) inherits a `save()` that rewrites `team_id` to the canonical parent (`posthog/models/scoping/product_mixin.py:43-46`). `TaskRun` is a plain `models.Model` (`products/tasks/backend/models.py:1063`), `Task` does not inherit `RootTeamMixin` (`models.py:112`), and `SignalReport` / `SignalReportArtefact` are `UUIDModel`, which is a bare abstract model (`posthog/models/utils.py:61-69`). None of them canonicalize, so they keep the environment team id the request carried.
**Found:** the comparison is exact and has no canonicalization. `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` passes `repo_config.team_id` into the facade (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:191-196`), and `find_signal_implementation_run` returns `None` on `run.team_id != team_id` (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:505`). A child-environment run against a parent-scoped config never matches.
**Found:** signals rows are environment-scoped on purpose, so the mismatched pair is a normal configuration rather than a contrived one. `products/signals/backend/views.py:254-262` canonicalizes only the scout source config and states that all other sources stay environment-scoped.
**Found:** this explains why only the second leg breaks. The initial dispatch passes the raw `instance.team_id` (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:134`) and `process_inbox_pr_review` resolves the config through `StamphogRepoConfig.objects.for_team(team_id)` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1141`), which canonicalizes the incoming id. So the first review runs and the approval lands.
**Found:** the failure is worse than a silent no-op, and it misreports itself. With `carve_out.provenance` empty, a `synchronize` falls into the skip branch at `tasks.py:881-903`, which calls `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip` with `_UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE` and logs `stamphog_pr_event_skipped` with `reason=skip_reason` — the bot-author reason. The PR loses its approval, gets no re-review, and both the dismissal message and the log point an operator at author trust instead of at team scoping.
**Found (refinement):** the artefact-query half is downstream, not a second live defect. `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` is only reached at `tasks.py:201-205`, after the facade check at line 199 already established `run.team_id == repo_config.team_id`, so the query in `receivers.py:180-185` currently uses a matching id. It becomes wrong the moment the facade comparison is relaxed, which is exactly why the fix has to pass the raw `run.team_id` into the resolver rather than only loosen the ownership check.
**Impact:** confirmed correctness bug for any project that runs signals tasks from a non-root environment while its Stamphog config sits on the project root. Every push after the first review dismisses the standing approval and starts no replacement review.

title: Former project members can remain approval reviewers
problem: `resolve_org_github_login_to_users` checks organization membership only. It does not require an active user or current project access. A disabled user or former private-project member can retain an enabled setting. If their login remains assigned, this hook continues to queue approval-capable reviews.
suggestion: Resolve reviewers through a project-access-aware helper. Require active users from `Team.all_users_with_access()`. Add cases for account deactivation and private-project access removal.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** what the resolved user id actually confers on the Stamphog leg, whether any identity check already filters deactivated users, and whether org-membership resolution here is a local shortcut or a shared convention.
**Found:** on this leg the acting user id is provenance only. It is passed to the facade (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:132,152`), written into `ReviewRun.output["inbox_review"]["acting_user_id"]` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1176-1180`, `tasks.py:208-214`), and never read back for a decision — `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:175,237,451` consume only the truthiness of `inbox_review`. No grep outside those sites reads the id.
**Found:** the one identity that does confer capability already fails closed on deactivation. The sandbox LLM credential is minted under `repo_config.connected_by_user_id`, and `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:128-133` filters `is_active=True` and raises when that user is missing or deactivated. A deactivated acting reviewer cannot mint anything, cannot pick the GitHub identity, and cannot see the result.
**Found:** the review is gated at repo level independently of any reviewer's preference row. `process_inbox_pr_review` requires a `StamphogRepoConfig` that is `enabled=True`, has a non-blank `installation_id`, and has a `connected_by_user_id` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1153`) — an admin action, not a stale personal setting.
**Found:** org-membership resolution is the product-wide convention for this assignment set, not a local shortcut. `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` states it resolves logins "the same way those surfaces resolve them" (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:162-164`), and `resolve_org_github_login_to_users` is the same helper behind signals' Slack inbox notifications (`products/signals/backend/slack_inbox_notifications.py:184`), the signals reviewer APIs (`products/signals/backend/views.py:2134,2318`), `auto_start.py:302`, and ReviewHog's own author resolution (`products/review_hog/backend/temporal/activities.py:572`). Swapping only this call site to `Team.all_users_with_access()` would make the review gate disagree with the Inbox "For you" filter and the Slack fan-out, which would still list the same person.
**Impact:** the mechanics described are accurate — there is no `is_active` or project-access filter, and a stale preference row survives — but the consequence does not reach the bar. No capability accrues to the departed or deactivated person, no tenant boundary is crossed, and nothing is disclosed to them. The residual effect is that automated review of the team's own self-driving PRs continues in a repository the team's admin connected and enabled, which is what the org opted into. Against a proposed fix that desynchronizes this gate from every other surface resolving the same set, this is preference hygiene rather than a permission gap.

title: The opt-out path leaves the old review workflow active
problem: This path dismisses stored approvals but does not supersede queued or reviewing runs. An older workflow can check the head before a push, then approve after this path returns.
suggestion: Mark all nonterminal ReviewRun rows for the pull request as SUPERSEDED before returning. This lets the existing post_verdict guards stop the old workflow.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the skip branch at `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:881-912`, the helper it calls, the sibling retraction path, and all three `post_verdict` guards.
**Found:** the premise holds — `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:483-516`) only calls `dismiss_stale_approvals_for_head`; no skip path calls `_supersede_prior_runs` (`:415-432`). The sibling retraction for a base retarget does supersede in-flight runs and states the reason at `:441-450`, so the asymmetry is inside this same file.
**Found:** the race survives the first two guards but would be caught by the third. `post_verdict` reads the live head from GitHub (`products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:673-685`), so an old run normally aborts after a push — unless its fetch happened before the push landed. The final `superseded_now` read (`:697-713`) is a DB status read taken immediately before the GitHub write, added for exactly this class of window; marking the run SUPERSEDED on the skip path is what arms it.
**Found:** nothing later cleans up the orphan within that delivery. A run that posts the approval finishes as COMPLETED/APPROVED, which is a normal terminal, so the terminal orphan sweep does not apply, and the skip path starts no workflow, so `dismiss_stale_approvals`'s startup sweep never runs. The approval is pinned to the pre-push head and stands until some later head-changing delivery sweeps it through `posted_review_id`.
**Impact:** a stamphog approval can stand over commits it never reviewed — the invariant this product treats as primary — and the abandoned run also keeps a sandbox alive and can post a sticky comment after the reviewer opted out.
**Priority:** lowered to should_fix. The window requires the push to land inside `post_verdict`'s fetch-to-write span, the gap is pre-existing on every other skip path (untrusted author, disabled repo) rather than introduced here, and the next head-changing delivery retracts the orphan. That is narrower and more self-healing than must_fix implies, but the fix is small and mirrors the base-retarget path.

title: The opt-out dismissal misses GitHub-only approvals
problem: The dismissal helper only finds approvals with a saved posted_review_id. A worker can post an approval and stop before saving that ID. This path starts no workflow, so the GitHub-side orphan sweep never runs. The approval remains active after the push.
suggestion: Move the GitHub approval sweep into shared approval logic. On every skipped head change, dismiss this App's active approvals whose commit_id differs from the current head.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** what `dismiss_stale_approvals_for_head` actually queries, where the GitHub-side sweeps live, and every layer that gives a posted approval a DB trace.
**Found:** the premise is accurate. `products/stamphog/backend/logic/approvals.py:44-55` filters on `posted_review_id__isnull=False`, and its docstring says the sweep is keyed off `posted_review_id` alone. The sweep that can find an approval with no row at all lists the App's own active approvals and lives only inside the workflow — `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:523` in `dismiss_stale_approvals` and `:560` in `_sweep_orphan_approvals_at_terminal`. The skip branch starts no workflow, so neither runs.
**Found:** three existing layers already close the window this depends on. `post_verdict` persists the id immediately after GitHub accepts the review (`products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:747-753`); a retry re-enters, finds the active approval pinned to the run's head and adopts its id rather than posting again (`:734-742`); and a run that fails re-runs the GitHub-side sweep at its terminal (`:857`). A DB-invisible orphan therefore needs the worker to die inside the sub-second gap between the POST and the update, AND the activity never to retry to completion, AND the workflow never to reach its terminal handler.
**Found:** the exposure only persists while every later delivery also skips, because any delivery that does reach the workflow sweeps GitHub-side first. An opted-out self-driving PR is exactly such a case, since later pushes keep landing on this branch.
**Impact:** when it does happen the result is a standing approval over commits nobody reviewed, which is the invariant this product treats as primary, and the codebase confirms this orphan class is real — the workflow sweep exists specifically to catch an approval with no `ReviewRun` row.
**Priority:** lowered to consider. The gap is pre-existing on every skip path rather than introduced here, it needs a stacked failure past three deliberate safety nets, and the proposed remedy adds a GitHub review-list call to every skipped head-changing delivery for any PR stamphog has touched. It is worth recording, not worth blocking on.

title: Hosted bot predicate omits posthog-bot
problem: These lines say `posthog-bot` is refused at every layer. The hosted `_is_bot_authored()` predicate only checks `type == "Bot"` or a `"[bot]"` suffix. `github.py` records `posthog-bot` as a `User` machine account. `_review_skip_reason()` therefore lets these PRs reach workflow creation. The engine refuses them later, but Stamphog first spends GitHub calls and sandbox startup.
suggestion: Make `_is_bot_authored()` match `github.py::is_bot_author` and the Action job gate. Add a hosted test for `posthog-bot`. If these runtimes cannot share code, add an explicit machine-user list and a parity test.
validator:
**Validator:** - **Checked:** the three layers the doc names — the hosted pre-filter (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:124-127` `_is_bot_authored`, used at `tasks.py:229` inside `_review_skip_reason`), the engine (`tools/pr-approval-agent/github.py:79-89` `is_bot_author`, applied at `review_local.py:207` and refused at `review_local.py:324-325`), and the Action job gates (`.github/workflows/pr-approval-agent.yml:30,255,409`).
**Found:** the divergence is real. `github.py:64` keeps an explicit `_BOT_MACHINE_USERS = {"posthog-bot"}` set and `is_bot_author` matches it by login; the workflow gates repeat `user.login != 'posthog-bot'` three times. The hosted `_is_bot_authored` only tests `user.get("type") == "Bot"` or `"[bot]" in login`, and `posthog-bot` is a type `User` login with no `[bot]` suffix, so it returns False.
**Found:** the hosted path therefore continues past the pre-filter for a non-draft `posthog-bot` PR: `author_association` for an org machine user is `MEMBER`/`CONTRIBUTOR`, both inside `PAYLOAD_GATE_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATIONS` (`tasks.py:98`), `ReviewMode.ALL` is the default (`facade/enums.py:13-14`) so `_review_mode_skip_reason` does not stop it, and the write-permission gate passes for a bot that pushes to branches. The run row, the Temporal workflow, and the sandbox all start before `review_local.py:324` refuses.
**Impact:** the safety boundary holds — `self_driving` is False for such a PR (no inbox provenance is stamped, since `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` is only consulted when `skip_reason` is set), so the engine refuses and no approval is minted. The confirmed cost is a wasted GitHub permission call plus a sandbox and LLM run per `posthog-bot` PR on an ALL-mode repo, and a refusal comment on that PR. The AGENTS.md sentence at line 82 ("refused at every layer — the webhook pre-filter (`_review_skip_reason`)") is inaccurate for exactly the machine user line 90 names.
**Priority:** lowered to `consider`. The predicate gap is real and the doc overstates it, but nothing unsafe results, and the hosted predicate has the same body outside this branch — the diff documents the gap rather than creating it. It is a real-but-minor parity and doc-accuracy issue, not a `should_fix` defect.
